moves: Adjacent photos translate together on one horizontally clipped rail.
fixed: The heading, viewport, divider and supporting footer stay in place.
notice: The next photo comes into view while the place and surrounding context remain easy to read.
fits: Browse pictures inside a place or album surface with persistent labels. Use the separate UI adapter variant for inline conversation paging.
avoid: A stack that lifts or dismisses only its front photo needs independent layers and depth.

moves: The heading text glides within its own clipped band.
fixed: Photo positions, their crop, the heading backdrop and bottom caption hold still.
notice: The viewer can compare the same images while the title establishes a new emphasis.
fits: Reposition an editorial label over stationary evidence or retain a fixed gallery frame.
avoid: This leaves every picture unchanged. Use a rail when the viewer needs to see a new photo.

moves: Draft characters arrive in the composer, transfer into an outgoing blue bubble, and an incoming gray reply arrives after a pause.
fixed: The phone, conversation header, composer field and reading area stay in place.
notice: An outgoing request leads to an incoming answer. The quiet gap separates the two actors.
fits: Show a short request and reply in the same conversation, with composer send and inbound text.
avoid: A one-way delivery or a manual reply composition needs different event timing.

moves: The composer gains characters at uneven intervals as the caret advances.
fixed: The draft field, transcript, heading, and phone viewport are stationary.
notice: A person is building a draft before any message is sent.
fits: Show human input or let the viewer read the prompt as it is typed.
avoid: Typing implies human authorship and input. It misreads a reply that arrives whole.

moves: The draft box collapses toward its right edge while the outgoing balloon rises, slightly overshoots, then settles into its transcript slot.
fixed: The conversation heading, prior reply, and composer field stay fixed. The send control disappears at the trigger.
notice: The text the viewer just read in the field becomes a real outgoing message.
fits: Establish the exact send moment without cutting away from the conversation.
avoid: A send flight implies committing the draft. Avoid it while composing, reviewing, or receiving a message.

moves: Three dots lift and dim in staggered phases inside a stationary bubble.
fixed: The dots’ container, prior outgoing message, composer and heading.
notice: The recipient is working on a reply, with no text to read yet.
fits: A short conversational pause before the other person answers.
avoid: Typing dots imply a participant is composing. A loading job, completed result or explicit delivery state needs its own signal.

moves: The previous rows lift together. The complete incoming reply rises a shorter distance into the bottom slot.
fixed: The header, composer, and bottom resting line of the transcript.
notice: The other participant has answered and the conversation advances to the latest message.
fits: A reply arrives in an already populated conversation.
avoid: A composer send, timestamp peek, or an answer generated a word at a time reads as a different action.

moves: The old receipt fades under the first bubble. The latest bubble rises toward its final slot as its receipt resolves.
fixed: The first bubble, the composer and the conversation heading.
notice: The delivery status belongs to the latest sent item.
fits: Track where a confirmation label lives after a new outgoing item is acknowledged.
avoid: A delivery confirmation does not establish that the recipient has read the message.

editProbes.heading: changes layer tree
editProbes.detail: Use Delivered, Read, or Failed for receipt detail in Clone iMessage UI

moves: Context dims while the option tray opens below the held row and the reaction rail grows above it.
fixed: The selected message stays centered on its original slot throughout the reveal.
notice: The press selects one message and exposes possible actions.
fits: Introduce options tied to a single message without implying a choice has happened.
avoid: A held menu should not imply a reaction was picked, content was deleted, or the full conversation changed.

moves: The selected reaction follows a curved approach, shrinks into a corner badge and settles as the nearby text row makes room.
fixed: Message copy, heading and composer. Earlier messages stay put.
notice: The chosen response belongs to this one message and remains attached after the picker goes away.
fits: Show the result of choosing a reaction once the available choices are understood.
avoid: A reaction overlay on the whole screen reads as celebration or product decoration.

moves: Every bubble shifts left once and springs back on release, exposing small times in a stationary gutter.
fixed: Times remain on the trailing edge. The heading, composer, and individual vertical positions stay fixed.
notice: These are times for existing messages, revealed by a temporary drag.
fits: Show when multiple parts of an existing conversation occurred.
avoid: This is a transcript-wide left drag. A single selected message moving right signals a reply gesture.

moves: Only the chosen bubble follows the drag. An arrow appears behind it, then the row returns and its quote opens above the composer.
fixed: Other transcript rows, header and reply input position.
notice: The next draft will reply to one specific earlier message.
fits: An answer needs an explicit target in a busy conversation.
avoid: A transcript-wide swipe to reveal timestamps never opens a quoted draft.

moves: A connector grows from the parent while two indented replies emerge in sequence. The next unrelated row moves down.
fixed: The parent message, heading and composer.
notice: Several messages belong under one earlier message, as a readable subthread.
fits: Expose a group of existing inline replies while preserving their parent context.
avoid: A quoted draft is an action the user will take next. It should not unfold a cluster of replies that already exist.

moves: The original bubble deepens to fit an editable second line. Nearby content reflows and the edit marker appears on commit.
fixed: The same message retains its identity and leading row. The header and main composer do not move.
notice: A previously sent message changes in place and keeps its row in the conversation.
fits: Correct existing text while preserving the surrounding conversation.
avoid: Do not show an edit by sending a second message or deleting the original row.

moves: The outgoing bubble contracts toward its own tail and fades. Nearby rows close the gap, then a quiet history status appears.
fixed: The header, composer and surviving messages’ copy.
notice: One previously sent message was retracted from the conversation.
fits: Show that a mistaken send was undone and what remains afterward.
avoid: This removal changes history. It is different from canceling an unsent draft or merely hiding one row for yourself.

moves: History appears above the visible rows. The rows stay put through insertion and then follow the next drag together.
fixed: The currently read bubble stays at the same position during insertion. The heading and composer remain fixed throughout.
notice: Earlier history became available while the current reading position was preserved.
fits: Demonstrate pagination or a chat-history fetch while keeping the viewer oriented.
avoid: Jumping to unread content deliberately changes the reading position and requires a destination marker.

moves: A single controlled scroll advances past intervening rows. The unread divider comes to rest at a predictable spot and the jump control clears.
fixed: The reading frame, composer and header stay anchored while the transcript travels.
notice: The destination is the beginning of unread content.
fits: Skip past older chat history and land on a marked new starting point.
avoid: Quietly fetching an earlier page should preserve the reading position and use a different move.

moves: The keyboard pushes up from below, lifting the composer and the last message to keep both reachable.
fixed: The conversation header and textarea contents. No characters are entered.
notice: The conversation moved into text-entry mode while preserving the latest message.
fits: Show how a reply starts and where the user will type next.
avoid: A keyboard rise should not be used as a visual synonym for typing or for sending a message.

moves: The link card extends horizontally and the source metadata slides in behind a clipping boundary.
fixed: The URL, message row height, adjacent reply, heading and composer.
notice: The shared link gained a richer preview alongside its original address.
fits: Play an inline metadata fetch or introduce information contained in an already shared link.
avoid: Opening this box is not navigation to the destination or a second message send.

moves: One outgoing bubble gives a short damped shake. The retry control and failure status then appear beside and below it.
fixed: Existing conversation rows, recipient, heading and composer.
notice: The message exists locally and delivery failed. The viewer can retry it.
fits: Demonstrate the recoverable failed-send state.
avoid: A failure signal should not shake the whole screen or confirm that the message arrived.

moves: A time wheel rolls behind a fixed selection band. The selected time persists in a small schedule chip as the wheel closes.
fixed: Selection band, draft copy and conversation history.
notice: The message will be sent later, at the time displayed on the chip.
fits: Make the distinction between choosing a send time and executing a send visible.
avoid: Do not use a send flight if this message stays in the draft area after scheduling.

moves: The transcript shifts to make room for a check rail. Two rows gain checks separately, then an action bar replaces the composer.
fixed: Header, transcript order, and each message’s text.
notice: Two particular rows are selected for a later shared action.
fits: Show deliberate selection across several messages before forwarding or deleting them.
avoid: Showing the batch controls does not imply the action was executed or affected every row.

moves: The avatar follows a short arc from its row into the pinned tray. Its old row collapses and lower rows slide up.
fixed: The inbox header, the pin lane, and other conversations’ names and preview copy.
notice: The same conversation is now reachable from the pinned area.
fits: Show a conversation being promoted within the inbox.
avoid: Pinning retains the conversation. It should not look like archiving, deleting or opening it.

moves: The camera plane scales around a chosen detail, taking its neighboring cards toward the edges.
fixed: The focal point, the cards’ arrangement within the camera plane, and the surrounding frame.
notice: The detail belongs to the same workspace established at the start.
fits: Lead into an important control or small result that was hard to read in the overview.
avoid: A push implies looking closer. Use a state change if the product itself opens or grows.

moves: A horizontal camera pan moves the view between adjacent panels. A small index marks the next destination.
fixed: Magnification, destination sizes and spacing, the viewing window, and the surrounding heading.
notice: The second view is next to the first on the same plane.
fits: Show a connection between adjacent panels or identify the next stop in an established horizontal layout.
avoid: A lateral camera move implies adjacency. A distant location needs a different transition.

moves: The foreground crosses quickly, the middle cards move a shorter distance, and the grid barely shifts.
fixed: The drawing window and the relative arrangement of objects on each plane.
notice: Different rates disclose depth between established planes.
fits: Reveal spatial layers or give a lateral product view a credible sense of depth.
avoid: Differential speed implies depth or independent planes. It can misstate a flat, rigid interface.

moves: Sharpness shifts from the near card to the far card. The near card softens in place.
fixed: Both cards’ positions and silhouettes, the frame, and the heading.
notice: The subject in the back becomes the point of attention even though its position never changes.
fits: Pass attention between subjects while preserving their positions and sense of depth.
avoid: Blur makes wording temporarily unreadable. Keep both clear for simultaneous comparisons.

moves: Letter spacing contracts toward the center without changing the word or type size.
fixed: The title’s center and baseline, its wording, and the axis underneath.
notice: Dispersed characters resolve into one readable phrase.
fits: Settle a short title at the end of a reveal, especially when the idea is convergence or agreement.
avoid: The initial tracking slows reading. Keep the spacing stable for long or urgent copy.

moves: An underline travels to the second step, holds, then travels to the third.
fixed: All step labels, the rail, and the explanatory line.
notice: The movement represents progression through an ordered set of stages.
fits: Show a workflow reaching successive checkpoints without moving the actual controls.
avoid: The indicator implies active progression. A set of unrelated options needs a different cue.

moves: Three values roll upward through a narrow clipped readout and stop at the final value.
fixed: Width and position of the readout, its baseline, and the metric label.
notice: One metric changes over time, with a marked starting value and a readable final value.
fits: Represent an increasing count or visibly changing ordinal state in an instrument-like readout.
avoid: A rolling readout suggests ordered progression. Keep unrelated labels out of a numeric roll.

moves: Both bars grow upward from the same baseline and stop at their own value.
fixed: The baseline, the target line, and the two category labels.
notice: The second bar clears the target line while the first falls short in the default example.
fits: Compare quantitative magnitudes with a shared reference and readable final state.
avoid: Bar growth emphasizes size. Unordered categories or different units should use a different treatment.

moves: A leading point traverses the chart and leaves the completed segments behind.
fixed: Grid lines, axes, and the endpoints of the plotted values.
notice: Ordering matters. The retained path makes the direction and reversals legible.
fits: Reveal how a trend developed across a series of points.
avoid: A traced path implies an ordered series. Use independent bars for unrelated categories.

moves: Each card follows an individual path into a changed grid order.
fixed: Card copy and proportions, the board, and the heading.
notice: The same cards survive the layout change, even as reading order shifts.
fits: Make a changed sort or rearranged layout clear without losing track of the items.
avoid: A reflow suggests continuity of the existing set. If new items replace old ones, show that replacement.

moves: The first row grows down, its indicator rotates, and the following row makes space below it.
fixed: The top edge of the first row, the row titles, and the surrounding viewport.
notice: The details belong to the opening row, and the lower row remains part of the layout.
fits: Show details disclosed inside a vertically stacked list with physical reflow.
avoid: The push down implies that the content occupies layout space. Use an overlay for temporary detail.

moves: Three stacked planes spread diagonally, keeping a shared orientation as their edges separate.
fixed: Each layer’s own geometry, border, and label.
notice: The assembly contains separate working surfaces that belong together.
fits: Explain how a view is composed or which layer handles each responsibility.
avoid: The offset stack implies an assembly. Independent products should not look like layers of one interface.

moves: A bounded opening in a dim overlay travels from one phrase to the next.
fixed: All the text, its position, type, and spacing. The overlay keeps its height.
notice: The next phrase becomes current while earlier context stays visible in low contrast.
fits: Direct the eye to different phrases in a fixed diagram or copy layout.
avoid: Moving a spotlight reduces contrast outside the window. Use uniform contrast when the viewer must read all content at once.

moves: Two signals travel along separate pathways and combine at the junction. One outgoing packet continues along the shared route.
fixed: The branch geometry, junction, endpoints and labels.
notice: Independent inputs are combined before the result is delivered.
fits: Explain joins, aggregation, or collaboration with a clear point of convergence.
avoid: A single outgoing marker implies a real merge. Use separate paths if the inputs reach distinct results.

moves: Thin rings grow out from one source and fade at successive distances.
fixed: The source itself, heading, and explanatory text.
notice: A single originating action propagates outward to its surroundings.
fits: Show broadcasting, discovery, or a ripple of system activity from one source.
avoid: Radial expansion implies broad propagation. Use a routed movement for a directed delivery.

moves: Peripheral activity stops mid-travel. One point in the center keeps moving to its destination.
fixed: The tracks stay fixed throughout. After the stop, all peripheral points hold their exact positions.
notice: One process remains relevant while competing activity pauses.
fits: Isolate a still-running process in a dense animated wash of other activity.
avoid: Arresting activity changes the perceived system state. If all processes are running, use a highlight that preserves them.

moves: Each item takes a short arc into a counter, shrinks away at arrival, and advances the count.
fixed: The count surface, the label underneath it, and the overall framing.
notice: Every count increase corresponds to one specific arriving item.
fits: Show completion, aggregation, or the number of processed items.
avoid: A disappearing item implies conversion into a summary. Keep entities in separate cards when they still matter individually.

moves: An abrupt cut changes the surrounding shot in one frame. The supporting line appears after the cut.
fixed: The matched action shape, its position and size, and the action wording.
notice: A corresponding action connects two different contexts.
fits: Jump between two contexts while keeping a strong visual point of correspondence.
avoid: The cut implies editorial correspondence. Use a continuous transition when physical continuity matters.

moves: The objects travel toward each other, disappear behind a central cover, and emerge on opposite sides.
fixed: The central cover, both travel lanes, and the heading.
notice: The objects continue behind the cover and keep their identities as they reappear.
fits: Demonstrate a handoff through an occluded region or passage on the same plane.
avoid: A temporary disappearance can imply travel through a real intervening space. Use a dissolve for unrelated replacements.

moves: A single meter pointer rotates about its pivot, overshoots briefly, and settles at the desired reading.
fixed: Gauge ticks, the threshold region, the pivot and the labels.
notice: The shown value falls at a specific point on a bounded scale.
fits: Show one metric crossing a threshold or resolving into a stable reading.
avoid: A gauge implies a meaningful range. Use a cycle or spinner for activity that has no bounded reading.

moves: Conversation tiles enter in a stagger while a common camera glides through the wall.
fixed: The cells retain their columns; the layout order and each message identity stay readable.
notice: Independent examples accumulate into breadth.
fits: Show that a product works across distinct conversations or cases.
avoid: A single thread with new messages needs sender and timing continuity.

moves: The drawer carries a handle and icons upward together from offscreen.
fixed: The phone header and underlying message remain in place.
notice: The app choices live in a single drawer within the conversation.
fits: Reveal where to find a set of tools or integrations.
avoid: Opening an individual card into its own content is not a picker.

moves: The surface changes radius, size, and color while two distinct marks exchange at its center.
fixed: The central identity anchor and background plane hold.
notice: The viewer reads the new mark as the same product in a new form.
fits: Introduce an app icon as another expression of an existing identity.
avoid: When the icon is unrelated to the prior mark, a hard identity change reads more clearly.

moves: One circle widens into a panel while the corner radius changes; contents appear after the surface has room.
fixed: The transformation remains centered on the same stage anchor.
notice: The same surface becomes a place to act.
fits: Connect a compact affordance with the larger panel it opens.
avoid: A newly introduced unrelated surface should have its own arrival.

moves: An embedded card scales from its bottom anchor into reading size inside its conversation.
fixed: The request, composer, phone silhouette, and conversation header hold.
notice: The short request and a usable response coexist in the same surface.
fits: Show an inline app that remains in the thread while it grows.
avoid: A sheet that covers the conversation needs depth and scrim behavior.

moves: One control transitions from action color to pressed styling to confirmation wording and color.
fixed: The button position, geometry and parent card stay fixed.
notice: The same action visibly succeeds without a route change.
fits: Confirm a selected option or a completed action in the existing control.
avoid: A queued or uncertain outcome should not be signaled as complete.

moves: Independent cards arrive from separate angles with distinct rotations and settle into an ordered row.
fixed: The destination row establishes a common baseline against a stationary field.
notice: Distinct offerings become a set while retaining their labels.
fits: Introduce a small product family with breadth and comparable visual weight.
avoid: An avatar ring or a deck swipe implies a different spatial relationship.

moves: The top card translates and rotates off the deck; the next card advances in depth and turns back toward zero.
fixed: The attachment count, conversation label, composer, and backdrop remain fixed.
notice: The photos are separate cards in one attachment, and the next card moves into the lead slot.
fits: Show one-at-a-time browsing with an authored inline stack of overlapping attachments.
avoid: A horizontal media rail needs a shared strip translation with no individual promotion.

moves: A distinct grabber and sheet rise together and settle while the chat dims below.
fixed: The header and underlying message/card stay put in the conversation.
notice: The selected card opens another surface while the thread remains visible underneath.
fits: Expose more detail or actions in a temporary sheet while preserving conversation context.
avoid: An inline card expanding in place or an app-drawer picker has different content and layer ownership.

moves: Portraits approach on separate trajectories, sharpen and settle around shrinking headline copy.
fixed: The center of the copy remains anchored and the backdrop holds.
notice: Independent people converge around a shared idea without shifting the idea’s anchor.
fits: Present a group or set of participants around one promise.
avoid: Present products in a lineup if readers need to compare each with equal prominence.

moves: A perforated seam parts left to right as the stub tilts around the still-joined edge, then drops once detached.
fixed: The main ticket, its copy and the backdrop stay pinned.
notice: The smaller section belonged to the original ticket and is now independently usable.
fits: Show a detachable stub or one part becoming independent after separation.
avoid: An ordinary close action has no physical seam, and a stack reveal keeps its surfaces intact.

moves: A dot leaves the inline location cue, travels into the map, and compresses before it becomes an anchored pin.
fixed: The question, stage map, route, and heading remain stationary throughout the travel.
notice: The viewer connects the original question to an exact place on the map.
fits: Turn an address or a location answer into a physical destination while preserving the related question.
avoid: For unrelated destinations, use separate labels and a camera move rather than a single traveling token.

moves: The chosen thumbnail grows and moves into a raised preview while its neighbors dim.
fixed: The other thumbnail boxes, heading, footer, and viewport hold position.
notice: The same selected image is now large enough to inspect.
fits: Open one attachment while preserving its identity and origin in the row.
avoid: For a pinch in a fixed frame, use photo-pinch-detail. For a temporary long-press preview, use attachment-peek-release.

moves: The picture scales around a focal point inside a clipped viewer as the gesture markers spread.
fixed: The image window, control below it, heading, and footer hold position.
notice: The viewer is magnifying the picture inside an existing viewport.
fits: Give a viewer a closer look while preserving interface context.
avoid: For a whole-screen camera push or a thumbnail opening into a viewer, choose the corresponding camera or open motion.

moves: An oversized picture eases sideways underneath a stationary portrait crop frame.
fixed: The crop bounds, grid lines, heading, and footer hold position.
notice: The same image is composed around a different focal point at the same magnification.
fits: Demonstrate shifting a subject within a thumbnail crop or portrait frame.
avoid: For a series of different photos sliding by, choose a gallery strip. For changing magnification choose photo-pinch-detail.

moves: A divider increases the visible fraction of the second image from the same crop origin.
fixed: Both photo grids, the surrounding crop frame, and the outside controls hold position.
notice: The viewer can compare the two conditions at the same coordinate.
fits: Compare two versions of the same asset. Supply equally sized and registered before and after images.
avoid: For paging to a different photo or repositioning an image inside the crop, choose a gallery or crop reframe.

moves: The three already stacked thumbnails separate on staggered paths and straighten into a row.
fixed: Heading, footer, and the album label hold position.
notice: The individual images belong to the same combined attachment.
fits: Unpack a small set of photos from a single visible stack.
avoid: For navigating a photo rail beyond the visible area or changing an album grid density, use the respective rail or density move.

moves: The playhead drags forward, pauses, and backtracks; the sample shown in the fixed viewer follows its position.
fixed: The preview frame, timeline baseline, and interface chrome hold position.
notice: Moving through time changes the viewer while the rest of the UI remains stable.
fits: Show seeking instead of playback. Supply ordered stills from the same video as sample frames.
avoid: For selecting start and end boundaries, choose media-trim-range. The example samples are discrete images.

moves: The two range handles advance inward in separate gestures around a fixed filmstrip.
fixed: The filmstrip image positions, heading, footer, and time axis hold position.
notice: Only the section between the handles will be kept.
fits: Set in and out points, with excluded time still visible for orientation.
avoid: For jumping to a playhead location without changing the committed range, use media-video-scrub.

moves: One attachment rises and grows a little during a hold, then settles into exactly the original grid slot.
fixed: Neighboring thumbnails and interface chrome hold position.
notice: The viewer is temporarily inspecting an item before letting go, with no navigation or selection committed.
fits: Show a transient peek and return to the same spatial context.
avoid: For a committed large viewer, use photo-open-continuity. For moving an item to a new slot, use card-reorder-insert.

moves: The lifted tile follows a path over the row, its neighbors shift into the vacated space, and it docks in the new order.
fixed: The thumbnail row bounds, heading, and footer hold position.
notice: The dragged item is now third and the displaced items keep their relative order.
fits: Demonstrate a persistent order change in a set of editable media.
avoid: For a temporary lift with no order change, use attachment-peek-release. For bulk layout changes, use photo-grid-density.

moves: Successive bands sharpen over a soft version of the same photo.
fixed: The picture geometry, window, heading, and footer hold position.
notice: The visible asset is gaining detail rather than being replaced.
fits: Show a deliberately staged placeholder-to-full-resolution transition.
avoid: For a loading bar without pixel changes, use attachment-download-progress. For a reveal across previously empty space, use photo-iris-reveal.

moves: The caption window gains height, the full caption appears, and the neighboring row below is pushed down.
fixed: The photo bounds, disclosure control, heading, and footer hold position.
notice: The caption is part of the photo’s layout and takes up real space.
fits: Expose longer notes while keeping the photo visible and preserving a coherent layout.
avoid: For an overlay that should leave the rows underneath alone, use a modal or peek motif.

moves: A circular mask expands from a chosen point and opens to all four corners of the frame.
fixed: The underlying picture geometry, reveal origin, crop frame, and interface chrome hold position.
notice: The first detail appears at the chosen point; its surroundings are revealed from the same unmoving image.
fits: Reveal one image outward from an editorial focal point after a hold.
avoid: For a centered zoom where the photo itself changes size, choose photo-pinch-detail.

moves: The departing right leaf compresses toward the seam; its reverse side opens over the left page.
fixed: The album cover and center seam hold position, and content on resting pages has no free translation.
notice: The viewer advances to the next spread by turning one physical leaf.
fits: Present an album as a book; this is a flat hinge projection with shadow, without a rolling paper deformation.
avoid: For side-scrolling loose photos, choose a rail or a photo stack. For a whole card flipping independently, use a card flip.

moves: Existing images shrink and converge to new rows and columns while secondary tiles appear in the now reachable cells.
fixed: The grid region, headings, and footer hold position.
notice: The same album now shows more thumbnails per row while preserving item identity and order.
fits: Preview a grid density change, keeping the first four image identities across both states.
avoid: For a single dragged tile changing order, choose card-reorder-insert. For scaling a single picture without relayout, choose photo-pinch-detail.

moves: A determinate progress bar fills with two pauses; the status becomes available only at completion.
fixed: The attachment thumbnail, filename, card geometry, and interface chrome hold position.
notice: The item is still transferring until it reaches completion.
fits: Show a measured percentage advancing toward an openable attachment.
avoid: For waiting with unknown progress, choose an indeterminate indicator. For a progressively sharpening image, use media-progressive-sharpen.

moves: A curved annotation accumulates in drawing order with the pen tip moving along the growing stroke.
fixed: The photograph, viewport, heading, and footer hold position.
notice: The markup singles out a region while keeping the underlying photo visible.
fits: Direct attention with a hand-drawn path that remains at the end of the move.
avoid: For gradually exposing the photo itself, choose a reveal. For following a real contour, replace the editable markup coordinates to match that subject.

moves: The lower camera pushes toward a location control; the keyboard and composer clear, and a map occupies their former region.
fixed: The question remains the readable anchor. It nudges with the camera push, then holds through the change of surfaces.
notice: The map is the direct answer to the same location question, and the empty interval gives the change room to read.
fits: Carry a specific question across composer action and visual answer, retaining the question as the bridge.
avoid: Use a traveling pin when the physical token itself has to trace the correspondence.

moves: The phone falls away to the left and loses focus as the physical prop on the right sharpens. The camera cuts to a tighter continuation, pushes in a little farther, then holds.
fixed: The prop stays put on the table. The reply and its conversation layout move together with the phone.
notice: The reply names something that exists outside the phone, and the tighter shot confirms it is the same physical object.
fits: Use when a readable message identifies a physical object and the next beat needs the audience to recognize that object in the real scene.
avoid: Moving attention off the phone ends that reading beat. A long reply or text that still drives the next action needs a longer read or a later cut.

moves: Only the numeric value steps through intermediate whole numbers, then the final value holds.
fixed: The heading, metric label, optional unit and field stay in place.
notice: Readable growth or reduction on one comparable measure while the label retains its meaning.
fits: Count one metric up or down between known endpoints without scrolling its digits.
avoid: An odometer needs rolling glyphs. Use a still when only a final value is supported.

moves: Unsettled character slots change while their positions stay fixed, then resolve into a readable title left to right.
fixed: The title field, heading and camera hold steady.
notice: A title changes from unreadable to definite without moving the reading position.
fits: A short decode, establishment or reveal where delayed legibility is intentional.
avoid: Keep accessibility-critical or instructional text readable from its first frame.

moves: Two separate picture planes slide outward in opposite directions and open a gutter for a label.
fixed: The original frame and revealed text stay centered.
notice: Two distinct views make room for a shared conclusion between them.
fits: The pair and the central conclusion should remain simultaneously visible.
avoid: A wipe replaces one field with another. Use that for an in-place before/after comparison.

moves: The outer leaves rotate in opposite directions around a common pin and stop in a standing fan.
fixed: The center leaf, visible pivot, heading and camera are fixed.
notice: The surfaces are variants of the same collection and share a single attachment point.
fits: Reveal three material or visual samples simultaneously around an anchored pivot.
avoid: A stack swipe removes a top item. Use it when only one item should be active at a time.
